# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

## Plan (plan_complete)

Decomposed into 8 child work items (test-first / vertical-slice), all at
stage `intake_complete`:

**Phase 1 — Foundation**
- Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock module (AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ)

**Phase 2 — Grid + invariant**
- Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG)
- Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing (AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**
- Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A)
- Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire (AH-0MUGY7ZUO008QSUX)

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**
- Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ)
- Update documentation: GDD sections, README, code comments (AH-0MUGY8DPC005ERM9)
- Run full test suite and fix any failures (AH-0MUGY8HHU006XMU9)

**Dependency edges:** T2→T1, T3→T1, T4→T3, T5→{T1,T2}, T6→T4,
T7→{T2,T3,T4,T5}, T8→{T6,T7}.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every implementation task carries its own

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

# Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator

## Problem statement

The Enemy Gym configurator exposes a slider for every shot-behaviour field
except bullet time-to-live (TTL), even though `EnemyConfig.bulletLifetime` is
already a persisted CSV column and is plumbed through the entity firing seam.
As a result a designer cannot tune TTL from the gym, and the difficulty scorer
ignores TTL entirely — an archetype that sprays long-lived bullets (which wrap
the screen and stay lethal) is scored identically to one whose bullets expire
almost immediately. This work item closes both gaps: a TTL slider in the enemy
configurator, and TTL as a positive contributor to the enemy difficulty index
(higher TTL ⇒ higher difficulty).

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — tunes enemy bullet lifetime from the
  Enemy Gym and immediately sees the effect on the live difficulty readout.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs the difficulty model to account for bullet
  persistence so the campaign ordering stays auditable as archetypes are
  retuned.

Example user stories:

- *As a level designer, I want a TTL slider in the Enemy Gym enemy panel, so
  that I can tune how long enemy bullets persist without editing the CSV by
  hand.*
- *As a level designer, I want the difficulty score to rise when I increase
  TTL, so that a long-lived-bullet archetype is measured as harder than the
  same archetype with short-lived bullets.*
- *As a reviewer, I want the campaign difficulty ordering to remain
  non-decreasing after TTL is added as a factor, so that the intended
  progression cannot silently invert.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — TTL slider in the enemy configurator.** The `GymEnemies` editor panel
  renders a `bulletLifetime` range slider, queryable as
  `input[data-config="bulletLifetime"]`, with a documented min/max/step
  (proposed 0.1–5.0 s, step 0.1 — see Assumptions). It is seeded from the
  active config, updates its value readout and the in-memory `currentConfig`
  on input, and persists through both **Save** and **Save As…** (round-trips
  via the CSV store).
- **AC2 — TTL live-applies to spawned enemies.** Changing the slider
  live-applies the new TTL to already-spawned entities through the existing
  `_bulletLifetime` seam (no respawn required), consistent with the other
  shot-behaviour sliders.
- **AC3 — TTL is a difficulty factor (higher TTL ⇒ higher difficulty).**
  `enemyDifficulty` adds a `bulletLifetime` entry to `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` and
  `FACTOR_RANGES`, normalised so a longer lifetime scores higher. The factor
  appears in both `breakdown` and `factors`, and contributes **zero** when
  firing is suppressed (`shotPattern === 'none'`, or `suppressFiring: true` /
  waves with `shootEnabled: false`), matching the other firing factors.
- **AC4 — Validation tests.** Unit tests assert that increasing `bulletLifetime`
  never decreases the enemy score, that the factor is suppressed for
  non-firing archetypes, and that `breakdown`/`factors` include the new key.
  Scene-level tests cover the slider (present, range, seed, live-apply,
  difficulty-readout change, Save/Save As round-trip). The campaign calibration
  test (`src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`) must still pass — the
  built-in campaign ordering stays non-decreasing.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated.** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §9.2 factor table gains the `bulletLifetime` row (weight, range, inverted?
  no — longer is harder) and §9.4's per-archetype/campaign score tables are
  recomputed. Code comments on the new factor explain the direction and
  suppression rule. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No CSV/format change.** `bulletLifetime` is already a persisted column
  (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with codec support — do not add a new field or
  break round-trip compatibility.
- **Absolute, deterministic, 0–100.** The difficulty model stays independent of
  player state; weights and ranges remain named constants in one place, and
  tests pin **ordering/monotonicity**, not magic numbers.
- **Weight choice changes the published campaign scores.** Adding a factor
  changes `WEIGHT_SUM`, so the documented §9.4 tables must be recomputed and
  the campaign ordering re-verified.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.
- Scope discipline: extra opportunities (e.g. making the Boss archetype honour
  `bulletLifetime` instead of the fixed `BOSS_BULLET_LIFETIME`, or adding a
  player-bullet TTL control) are recorded as linked follow-ups, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig.bulletLifetime: number` already
  exists (documented "Bullet lifetime in seconds").
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed lifetimes: scout/diver/swarm/asteroid
  1.5 s, tank/boss 2.0 s, phaser 1.75 s.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — `bulletLifetime` column present with the above
  values; `src/core/csv.ts` already parses/coerces it.
- `src/entities/*` — Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm all accept
  `bulletLifetime` via `BaseEnemy` (default 1.5 s) and stamp it onto fired
  bullets. **Boss ignores the config value** and uses the module constant
  `BOSS_BULLET_LIFETIME = 2.0`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES` lists every numeric
  shot/formation field **except** `bulletLifetime`; `_applyLive` already
  patches `_bulletLifetime` is *not* present (only `_bulletSpeed`,
  `_fireInterval`, `_burstCount`, `_shotProbability`, etc.).
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`/`FACTOR_RANGES` cover nine
  factors (`count`, `driftSpeed`, `shotPattern`, `fireInterval`,
  `shotProbability`, `bulletSpeed`, `burstCount`, `formationKind`,
  `asteroidSplit`); firing factors are zeroed when suppressed.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §9 documents factors, ranges and
  the recomputed campaign table.

## Desired change

1. Add `bulletLifetime` to `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES` in `GymEnemies.ts`
   (0.1–5.0 s, step 0.1 proposed), placed after `bulletSpeed`. It flows through

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.
- The campaign fire rule is derived from the (1-based) level number: `level <= 3` ⇒ `shootEnabled=false`, `level >= 4` ⇒ `true`. With a data-driven skeleton this applies to any configured levels beyond 5 as firing levels; per-level `shootEnabled` overrides are out of scope.
- "Configurable curve" is satisfied by the CSV-backed config plus the baked-in default; runtime UI editing is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL.

## Acceptance criteria

- **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
- **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths).
- **Runtime generation runs** — at run start, with the toggle enabled, the game builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- **CSV-backed, data-driven config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` defines level number, level name and per-wave targets (curve length ⇒ wave count); it is loaded through the existing CSV/configStore pipeline and is editable in dev / read-only in production. Malformed or missing rows fall back to the baked-in default curve without crashing.
- **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what `PlayScene` spawns (verified via the spawn plan / `WaveManager.planSpawns()` or a test harness), not the static `LEVELS`.
- **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).

- `src/core/csv.ts` — add a difficulty-curve codec (parse/serialize + validation, mirroring `EnemyConfig`).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the difficulty-curve row/config types (leaf module, no imports).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — load `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing dev/bundled pipeline and expose an accessor.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` tunable (default `false`) to `GameRules`.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

- **CSV pipeline scope** — extending the codec/plugin/store is the largest cost; mitigated by mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec/plugin exactly and reusing the generic write endpoint where possible.
- **Default-curve calibration drift** — seeding from measured `LEVELS` scores could diverge from the static campaign if either changes; mitigated by a test asserting the default generated campaign is non-decreasing and stays in 0–100.

- Runtime curve editing UI (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).

- Per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD).

- **Q (Round 1): Does the generated sequence replace `LEVELS` outright, or sit behind a toggle?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) opt-in, default off** — shipped behaviour stays unchanged until a designer enables it. Additionally the operator asked for a follow-on work item allowing a campaign to **mix generated and scripted levels**.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Follow-up: created **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)**.

  - Answer (operator): **(b) per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: the sequencer takes a single `defaultShootEnabled` for a whole call and returns one group per curve entry — a whole-run curve cannot vary the fire rule by level. Read `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

- **Q (Round 1): Where does the curve (and its override) live?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) extend the CSV `configStore` with a new difficulty-curve file.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `configStore`/`csv.ts` are CSV-backed and read-only in production; `rules.ts` is the localStorage tunables store. Read `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts`.

- **Q (Round 2): When generated mode is enabled, does the campaign skeleton stay fixed?**

# Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the mineral kill-drop code with the game

## Headline

Gym asteroids do not drop minerals because the kill-drop rule lives only in the
game (`PlayScene`) while the gyms run a divergent copy. Extract the rule into one
shared helper used by both, and wire it into the gyms so they drop minerals
(small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) exactly as the game
does.

## Problem statement

Asteroids in the gym scenes do not drop minerals when destroyed, even though the
shipped game does and the gyms' own documentation says they should. The cause is
code divergence: the mineral **kill-drop** logic lives privately in `PlayScene`
and was never shared, while the gyms re-implemented the collection half of the
mineral layer and omitted the drop half. The fix is to make gym asteroids drop
minerals (per GDD §4.4.1) and to move the kill-drop logic into a single shared
helper used by both the game and the gyms, so the two can no longer drift.

## Users

- **As a player using the minerals gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid I want
  it to leave a mineral, so the gym demonstrates the real mechanic I see in the
  game.
- **As a player using the asteroid enemy gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid
  I want it to drop a mineral, so the gym matches the game's asteroid behaviour.
- **As a developer**, I want the mineral kill-drop logic to exist in exactly one
  shared place, so a gym and the game can never again disagree about whether an
  asteroid drops a mineral.
- **As a player**, when a non-asteroid enemy that has absorbed minerals is
  destroyed, I want it to re-drop a fraction of them, in the gym as in the game.

## Root cause (RCA summary)

- The shared base `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` provides the generic
  destruction seam (`onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` → `onEnemyDestroyed`) but has no
  mineral concept.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` overrides `onEnemyDestroyed` and, in the private
  `_onEnemyKilled()`, implements the drops: small asteroid → `spawnMineralAt()`;
  large/medium asteroid → none (split children drop); non-asteroid enemy →
  `entity.spawnMineralDrops()` (25–50 % re-drop).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` re-implements the mineral layer
  (`seedMinerals`, `_initMineralLayer`, `_updateMinerals`) but its
  `onEntityDestroyed` path only splits asteroids — it never spawns a mineral and
  never calls `spawnMineralDrops()` on death.
- `GymMinerals.ts` (asteroids-only) and `GymEnemies.ts` (generic enemy gym, used
  for the "Asteroid" config row) both extend `GymFormationScene`, so both are
  affected.
- Prior unification work (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO) shared the combat core but left
  the mineral logic duplicated — exactly the divergence the operator suspected.
- The gym docstrings and GDD §6.4 already claim "small-asteroid mineral drops …
  enemy absorption/re-drop"; the earlier gym item (AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB) had this
  in its acceptance criteria but it was closed without the drop behaviour.

## Existing state

- `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount()` / `spawnMineralDrops()` already implement the
  25–50 % re-drop and are unit-tested (AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA / AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM).
- `PlayScene.spawnMineralAt()` is public and used by the game and, in principle,
  by gyms.
- `Asteroid.collectMineral()` is a no-op (asteroids are inert to minerals) and
  `Asteroid.getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()` exist.
- `GymFormationScene` already owns a mineral field, a hold, a HUD counter and the
  hold-full choice overlay, and seeds 100 minerals on create.
- The rules config exposes `mineralCollectAmount`, `mineralHoldCapacity`,
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max`.

## Desired change

- Extract the mineral kill-drop rule into one shared helper used by **both**
  `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` (and therefore every formation gym).
  The helper decides, for a destroyed enemy, how many minerals to spawn and
  where: small asteroid → exactly one at the death site; large/medium asteroid →
  none; non-asteroid enemy → the configured fraction of minerals absorbed,
  scattered at the death site.
- Wire the helper into the gym destruction path so gym asteroids (and other
  gyms' enemies) drop minerals exactly as the game does.
- Leave gameplay values and balance unchanged; reuse the existing rules tunables.
- Keep the game's observable behaviour identical (pure refactor there), and keep
  the existing mineral tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid
  in `GymMinerals` and in the `GymEnemies` asteroid-config row spawns exactly one
  mineral at the asteroid's position (matching `PlayScene`). Large/medium
  asteroids do not drop directly; their small split children do. Verified by a
  scene test that destroys a small asteroid and asserts the live mineral count
  increases by one at that position, and by a test that a large/medium asteroid
  splits without a direct drop.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid
  enemy that has absorbed minerals re-drops between the configured
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max` fraction of them (never more than collected)
  at its death site. Verified by a deterministic test injecting a seeded RNG.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid
  drop + non-asteroid re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper/module and
  consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`; `PlayScene`'s private
  kill-drop block delegates to it. Verified by a parity/equivalence test and by
  the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passing.
- **AC4 — No game behaviour regression.** `PlayScene` mineral behaviour
  (small-asteroid drop, non-asteroid re-drop, collection, absorption, hold-fill
  choice) is unchanged; the existing `PlayScene` mineral tests stay green.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New/extended tests cover AC1–AC3 in the
  gym suites (`GymMinerals.test.ts`, `GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `GymFormationScene.test.ts`) and all pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4), the
  `GymMinerals`/`GymFormationScene` docstrings and any relevant README/docs
  entries describe the shared mineral kill-drop code and the gym behaviour.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes
  with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change balance/tuning values; use the existing rules config.
- Prefer a genuinely shared helper over per-scene copies (the operator selected
  the shared-helper approach); avoid introducing a second divergence.
- The extracted helper must not force gym-specific concerns (hold, HUD, choice)
  into the game, nor game-specific concerns (score, waves) into the gym.
- Tests must be meaningful and deterministic (TDD preferred); no snapshot-only
  or trivially-true assertions.
- Written output and docs in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — likely host for, or hook to, the shared
  mineral kill-drop helper (shared base of game and gyms).
- `src/scenes/core/<new mineral helper>.ts` (or `src/core/minerals.ts`) — the
  single shared implementation of the kill-drop rule.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — refactor `_onEnemyKilled()` mineral block to
  delegate to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — call the shared helper from the
  destruction path; add dropped minerals to the gym's mineral field.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — reuse `spawnMineralDrops()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — reuse `getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.1 / §6.4 wording and gym docstrings.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q` — parent mechanic (asteroids drop minerals; hold; choice).
- `AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB` — asteroids-only mineral gym; its AC claimed small-asteroid
  drops and enemy re-drop, but the drop half was not implemented (this item closes
  that gap).
- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — prior unification of PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat
  logic into a shared core; this item extends the same principle to minerals.
- `AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA` — mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count.
- `AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM` — tests for enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution.
- `AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT` — Mineral collectable entity and constants.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — ability items (Dual Shot/Teleport/Phase Shift) not
  functioning; a distinct gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared; a distinct
  gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the distinct gym-sharing defects `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (ability items)
  and `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` (enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating).
- Any change to mineral balance/tuning values or the hold/choice reward pool.
- Reworking the reward/choice flow itself; only the drop-on-kill wiring changes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the clean shared boundary is unclear because the game and gyms differ
  in hold/HUD/choice/score concerns. **Mitigation:** share only the field +
  collection/absorption + kill-drop mechanics, keep hold/score/choice in the
  scenes, and cover the seam with parity tests.
- **Risk:** scope creep into the two related gym-sharing defects
  (`AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4`, `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV`). **Mitigation:** keep those out
  of scope; they are separate work items.
- **Risk:** the refactor could change `PlayScene` behaviour subtly.
  **Mitigation:** AC4 requires the existing mineral tests to remain green and a
  parity test to pin the shared rule.
- **Assumption:** gyms should behave exactly like the game for mineral drops
  (operator confirmed the non-asteroid re-drop should be included).
- **Assumption:** the shared helper is the preferred approach over a local gym
  patch (operator selected the shared helper).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Non-asteroid enemy re-drop in gyms — include it, or asteroids only?" —
  **Answer (operator):** "Yes, include it." Source: interactive reply. Context:
  the re-drop mechanism already exists (`BaseEnemy.spawnMineralDrops`) but is not
  wired into gyms; including it keeps the shared path complete.
- Q: "Refactor boundary — shared helper used by both PlayScene and
  GymFormationScene, or a local gym patch?" — **Answer (operator):** "Shared
  helper." Source: interactive reply. Context: RCA confirms the divergence, so a
  shared helper prevents recurrence.
- Q (operator-initiated): "Check whether a work item exists for the previously
  raised issue about enemy drops; if so, close it." — **Answer/Research:** no
  open work item matching "enemy drops" exists in the worklog. All drop/mineral
  items are already `completed` (`AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q`, `AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB`,
  `AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM`, `AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA`, etc.). The only related *open*
  items are `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (ability items) and `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV`
  (enemy gym hit-gating), both distinct defects and left open. No item closed.

# Intake brief — Gym↔game behavioural-parity audit

**Headline:** A full evaluation of the scene layer found twelve places where the shipped `PlayScene` and the gym scenes still run **divergent copies of the same behaviour**. This epic tracks extracting each into one shared implementation (or explicitly recording an intentional difference), so that every object behaves identically in every scene and new divergence is caught by an automated guard.

## Problem statement

Operators continue to see errors caused by differences between gym scenes and the game scene. The producer directive is that **gyms and the game must execute the same core code**; the only legitimate difference is that a gym enables a **constrained set of features** (one enemy type, the enemy editor, fixed formations, no campaign/wave progression). Prior epics (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`, `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ`) unified the eight combat/lifecycle methods onto `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, but the audit below shows that a second tier of behaviour — player control, enemy fire dispatch, projectile lifecycle, power-up drops, minerals, the boss, teleport and the gym base seams — is still duplicated and has already drifted.

## Users

- **As a player**, when I practice in a gym I want every object (player, enemies, asteroids, boss, minerals, power-ups, bullets) to behave exactly as it does in the game, so the gym is a truthful training ground.
- **As a developer**, when I change a behaviour I want to change it in exactly one place, so a scenario cannot drift from the shipped game.
- **As a tester**, I want an automated parity guard that fails when a scene re-introduces a duplicate of a shared method, so regressions are caught before release.
- **As the producer**, I want the "gyms are the parity reference" principle enforced by code structure and tests.

## Evaluation method

Reviewed every production scene under `src/scenes` (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`/`GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) plus the shared cores `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, and the entity/config layer (`enemyFactory`, `BaseEnemy`, `Asteroid`, `Boss`, `Mineral`, `powerups/*`). Compared method inventories, dispatch tables, per-frame sequences and copy-pasted bodies, and cross-checked against the existing worklog so as not to duplicate open items.

## Findings — the gap register

| # | Gap | Evidence (divergent copies) | Impact |
|---|-----|------------------------------|--------|
| 1 | **Player-control step duplicated** | Input→timers→multipliers→physics sequence re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`; `GymPlayer.update` inlines the input-map branch instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput` | Player movement/fire-rate differs between scenes; GymPlayer does not share any control code |
| 2 | **Enemy fire dispatch duplicated** | `PlayScene._fireFor` and `GymEnemies.collectBullets` both hard-code `enemyKey → tryFire*`; `GymPowerUpsCombat._tickScouts` re-implements it again with a **fake fixed 16 ms clock** (`_nextFireTime += 16`) instead of the scene clock | A new enemy type must be wired twice; gym/combat fire cadence is frame-count-based, not time-based |
| 3 | **Projectile lifecycle duplicated** | Enemy-bullet wrap+expiry loop in `PlayScene._advanceBullets`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat._advanceEnemyBullets`; player-bullet advance via `advanceAndCull` in `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene._advancePlayerBullets`, `GymWeapons._advanceBullets`/`advanceBullets` | Wrap/expiry fixes reach one scene only |
| 4 | **Power-up drop layer duplicated & drifted** | Spawner build (`PlayScene._buildDropSpawner` ≈ `GymFormationScene._buildDefaultPowerUpSpawner`); lifecycle+collection (`PlayScene._updateDrops`/`_collectIfOverlapping` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updatePowerUpLayer`/`_collectOverlappingDrops` ≈ `GymWeapons.advanceDrops`/`collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsCombat.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsUtility.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping`); **P9 magnet** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsUtility`; **P4 bomb notice** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsCombat`; **per-type pickup cues** only in `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` | P9/P4/cue behaviour differs between gyms; five copies of the collect loop |
| 5 | **Mineral layer duplicated & drifted** | `PlayScene._handleMinerals` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updateMinerals`; `openMineralChoice`/`selectMineralChoice` duplicated with different contracts (`GameState` + overflow + `MineralChoiceScene{origin,options,strategy}` vs a local `mineralHold` capped and reset to 0 + `MineralChoiceScene{onSelect}`); `MineralChoiceScene` carries both interfaces | Hold overflow, choice wiring and reward application differ between game and gym |
| 6 | **Boss integration diverges** | `PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` runs inside `tick`; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` **then** advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick()` never advances the boss; `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies` avoids the boss for P7, `GymBoss` does not; `PlayScene._spawnMinions` (phase minions) has no gym equivalent | Boss behaves differently (bullet timing, teleport safety, minions) in the gym |
| 7 | **Teleport duplicated** | `GymPowerUpsCombat.triggerTeleport` is a full override of the shared `CombatScene.triggerTeleport`, bypassing `canTeleport()` and the hit-radius hooks (hard-codes `ENEMY_HIT_RADIUS`/`BULLET_HIT_RADIUS`) | Teleport safety logic can drift; the gym override is not exercised by shared tests |
| 8 | **Asteroid split duplicated** | Identical `onEntityDestroyed` split closures in `GymEnemies.ts` and `GymMinerals.ts` | A split-physics change must be made twice |
| 9 | **Gym base seams bypassed via casts** | `GymEnemies._onRespawn` reaches into private `entities`/`playerBullets` and re-implements `GymFormationScene._respawnFormation`; `_onTogglePlayer` casts to mutate the base's private `player`/spawn coords | Duplicate respawn logic; fragile casts |
| 10 | **Restart/teardown parity** | `PlayScene._resetRunState` calls `effectsRegistry.reset()`; `GymFormationScene` only recreates the registry when the power-up layer is enabled, and never resets it on teardown, so `GymMinerals`/`GymEnemies` keep permanent effects across a restart | Stale effects after restart in gyms without field drops |
| 11 | **GymPlayer not on the shared control core** | `GymPlayer` extends `Phaser.Scene` and inlines the scheme→input mapping; no shared player tick | The "player" object is the one object with a genuinely separate code path in one gym |
| 12 | **No automated parity guard for the second tier** | The existing `definesMethod` guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) covers only the original eight methods; none of the shared helpers above are guarded, and the cross-scene equivalence test covers only a subset of behaviours | Future divergence is invisible until a user reports a bug |

> **Already tracked (do not duplicate):** mineral **kill-drop** rule — `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (+ children `AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS`, `AH-0MUIG1AFG00938TV`, `AH-0MUIGTRVA0072TWW`, `AH-0MUIGTSAX00096Y4`, `AH-0MUIG16QK003MSNO`); "gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" — `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1`; beat-clock fire scheduling — `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (+ blocked children). These are referenced as related/blocking rather than re-created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression guard.** The repo-wide duplicate-body guard is extended to cover every newly shared method/helper, and a permanent test fails if any production scene re-introduces a copy.
- [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth:** extract genuinely shared behaviour; do not trade one duplication for another. A shared module must not force game-only concerns (score, waves, lives) into gyms, nor gym-only concerns (editor, fixed formations) into the game.
- **Minimum churn / surgical:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **Preserve public/test seams** (e.g. `getBullets`, `advanceBullets`, `getDrops`, `getCollectAnimations`, `spawnDrop`, `triggerTeleport`, `getPlayerHitCount`, help/back handles).
- **Generics/type-safety:** the shared core is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); additions must not weaken typing.
- **Determinism:** tests drive `tick(dt)`; shared behaviour must be driven by the supplied `dt` and the scene clock — no frame-count fake clocks.
- **UK English** in all written output and docs.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this item does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26 against HEAD)

- Shared cores exist: `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (input, auto-fire, drop collection) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (collisions, hits, teleport); `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` extend `CombatScene`; `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` extend `CombatCoreScene`.
- The eight-method duplicate guard and cross-scene equivalence tests live in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`; `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` hosts `definesMethod`/`collectProductionSourceFiles`.
- `GymEnemies` is the single config-driven enemy gym (one row per enemy config on the index); `GymMinerals` is asteroids-only; `GymBoss` is the dedicated 4-phase boss gym; `GymPlayer` is the bare-bones tuning scene.
- Entity classes (`Player`, `Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`, `Boss`, `Asteroid`, `Mineral`) are already shared; the divergence is entirely at the **scene integration** layer.
- Open related items: `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (mineral kill-drop), `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` (document parity principle), `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (beat-clock fire scheduling).

## Desired change

Extract/consume shared behaviour for gaps 1–11 and extend the guard for gap 12, via the dependency-ordered child items below. Do not redesign gym feature gating: a gym may still enable only a subset of features and disable others (e.g. scoring), but the code running for an enabled object must be the same code as the game.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — host shared player tick, projectile lifecycle, and teleport hooks.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — delegate duplicated bodies to the shared helpers.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume shared helpers; expose protected seams; reset registry.
- `src/scenes/gym/{GymEnemies,GymBoss,GymMinerals,GymPlayer,GymWeapons,GymPowerUpsCombat,GymPowerUpsUtility}.ts` — consume shared helpers, remove local copies/casts.
- `src/scenes/core/<new shared modules>.ts` — e.g. projectile lifecycle, power-up drop layer, mineral layer, enemy fire dispatch.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — shared enemy-fire seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — extend guard/equivalence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — over-abstraction.** Pushing gym-only features into the shared core couples the game to dev tooling. Mitigation: share behaviour only, keep features behind hooks/flags.
- **Risk — behaviour-change ambiguity.** Some divergences may be intentional. Mitigation: each is listed as an OPEN QUESTION below; the default assumption is "the game's behaviour is canonical" unless the producer says otherwise.
- **Risk — test churn.** Both scene suites reach into private internals. Mitigation: keep method names/visibility on the shared base; assert hooks/shared path rather than a class.
- **Risk — scope creep** into a full engine extraction (wave/level system, editor UI). Explicitly out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked items.
- **Assumption:** the shipped game is the canonical behaviour wherever a difference is found, except where an intentional divergence is already approved (e.g. `GymPowerUpsCombat` 0.8 s invulnerability).
- **Assumption:** gyms remain feature-constrained (no campaign/wave progression, optional scoring); "no difference" means no difference in the code path for enabled features, not "the gym must run the campaign".

## Related work

- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core (completed, epic).
- `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ` — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — Enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared (completed) — prior example of this class of defect.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — Ability items not functioning (completed) — prior gym/game divergence in choice rewards.
- `AH-0MUD9R4BA004WQEM` — Cross-scene equivalence tests and duplicate-body verification (completed).
- `AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M` — Restore gym-game parity RCA (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals (open) — the mineral kill-drop slice of gap 5.
- `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md (open) — supports AC6/governance.
- `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` — Bullets should fall on the beat (open) — touches gap 2's fire clock.
- `AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL` — Dev Utilities gym scene (open) — future consumer of the shared modules.

## Open questions (canonical-behaviour doubts)

1. **P9 Magnet in formation gyms** — the game and `GymPowerUpsUtility` pull drops toward the ship; `GymFormationScene` (enemy/minerals/boss) does not. Adopt the game behaviour everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
2. **P4 bomb notice** — game and `GymPowerUpsCombat` show "BOMB! Bullets cleared"; formation gyms do not. Adopt everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
3. **Per-type pickup cues** — game/weapon/utility gyms play per-type activation cues; formation gyms play only the generic chime. Adopt the game's cue set? *Recommended: yes.*
4. **Boss minions** — the game spawns phase minions (`planMinionSpawns`); `GymBoss` does not. Should the boss gym mirror minion spawning, or is that a deliberately constrained feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*
5. **`GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability** — 0.8 s (local hook) vs the game's 1.5 s. Keep the approved exception or converge? *Recommended: keep the hook but document it explicitly as an intentional, approved difference.*
6. **Gym field-drop cadence** — the game drops on a kill chance; gyms drop on a timer. These are different spawn *sources*; is sharing only the lifecycle/collection correct? *Recommended: yes — keep distinct sources, share lifecycle/collection/magnet/notice/cues.*
7. **Mineral hold overflow** — the game carries overflow (`collected − capacity`); the formation gym resets the hold to 0. Adopt overflow? *Recommended: yes.*
8. **GymPlayer scope** — should the bare-bones player gym consume the shared player-control tick/input, or stay deliberately minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.*
9. **Scoring in gyms** — gyms show `SCORE: n/a`. Confirm scoring remains a deliberately disabled feature (not a divergence to fix). *Recommended: yes, keep disabled.*
10. **Enemy-fire seam shape** — shared factory-level dispatcher vs a common `fire(now)` method on `BaseEnemy`. *Recommended: factory-level dispatcher (less invasive to the entity hierarchy).*

## Plan — child work items (dependency-ordered)

| # | Child item | Type | Priority | Depends on | Register gaps |

## Problem

Running the test-skill runner (`.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) from inside a linked agent worktree (the mandated implement workflow: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) fails with a `live_repo_mutation` error whenever another agent creates a worktree during the (multi-minute) test run — even though the suite itself passes (`failures: []`).

## Root cause

`snapshot_repo_state()` resolves the checkout via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which from a linked worktree returns the **worktree root**, not the shared repo root. `_parse_worktrees()` then computes `agent_root = <worktree-root>/.worklog/worktrees` — a path that does not exist inside a linked worktree — so the real agent worktrees under `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` are never added to `excluded_refs`. Any concurrent `git worktree add --track -b <branch>` is therefore reported as a mutation.

Additionally, `diff_snapshots()` applies `excluded_refs` only to the refs surface, not to `config`: the `branch.<name>.remote` / `branch.<name>.merge` keys written by `git worktree add --track` are reported as added config even from the main checkout, so the same false positive also reproduces there under concurrency.

## Steps to reproduce

1. From a linked worktree, run `python3 .pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --json --force`.
2. While it runs, create a worktree from the main checkout (e.g. `implement.py start` for another item).
3. Observe `live_repo_mutation` listing the concurrently-created `refs/heads/wl-*` ref and its `branch.*` config keys, with `success: false`.

## Impact

- `/skill:test` cannot reliably populate the audit full-suite cache from a worktree in a multi-agent environment.
- Every retry races the same way; under sustained concurrency the guard can never pass from a worktree.
- `implement.py finish` is unaffected (it calls `run_cached`/npm directly, not this runner), and this repo's pre-push hook only runs `wl sync`, so the gate is not currently a hard blocker — but the audit evidence path is degraded.

## Expected behaviour

Compute the agent-worktree exclusion root from the shared git dir (e.g. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` → main checkout) rather than `--show-toplevel`, and apply `excluded_refs` to the `config` diff as well as the `refs` diff.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Running the runner from a linked worktree while a concurrent worktree is created elsewhere reports `success: true` when the suite passes.
2. Refs and their associated `branch.<name>.*` config keys for worktrees under `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` are excluded from the mutation diff.
3. A genuine suite-caused mutation (fixture branch with no registered worktree, config rewrite, moved `dev`) is still detected and fails the run.

# Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader

## Goal

As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Desired behaviour

- New leaf types in `src/core/configTypes.ts`: `DifficultyCurveRow` carrying `level`, `levelName`, `wave` and `targetDifficulty` — no imports (keeps the Vite config loader free of `?raw` resolution).
- `src/core/csv.ts`: `DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, `parseDifficultyCurves`, `serializeDifficultyCurves` and `validateDifficultyCurveRow`, mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec (non-destructive validation; defaults for missing values).
- New `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` with a leading `#` comment and columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`, seeded from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty(LEVELS[i].waves).score`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

# Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions

## Goal

As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts.

Deliver a pure, deterministic builder module `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` that turns the difficulty-curve config into `LevelDefinition[]` by calling the read-only `sequencer()` once per configured level, converting each `ShootableWave` into a `WaveDefinition`, applying the campaign fire rule and falling back to static `LEVELS` whenever the input is empty or degenerate.

## Desired behaviour

- `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)`:
  - Groups rows by `level` ascending and orders each level's rows by `wave` ascending.
  - For each configured level, calls `sequencer(curve, candidates, { defaultShootEnabled: level >= 4 })`, receiving one `ShootableWave` per target and therefore one `WaveDefinition` per target (curve length ⇒ wave count).
  - Maps `ShootableWave.groups` (`AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`) to `WaveDefinition.groups` and sets `shootEnabled` from the campaign fire rule.
  - Uses the level name from config; the level count is data-driven.
  - Is deterministic: no RNG, no clock and no I/O — the same inputs yield identical output.
- Fallback: if rows are empty/missing, a level has no targets, or the candidate pool is empty, returns static `LEVELS` unchanged behind a single guard.
- Uses `defaultDifficultyCurves()` (derived from the measured `LEVELS` scores) and `defaultCandidatePool()` when config is absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Runtime generation runs — the builder builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- Generated waves drive the run — the groups produced by the sequencer are present in the returned `LevelDefinition[]` and flow through `WaveManager.planSpawns()` (verified via the spawn plan).
- Curve is configurable — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- Campaign fire rule — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- Determinism — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- Fallback is safe — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
- Pure core stays pure — `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).

## Out of scope

- Per-level `shootEnabled` overrides and per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD).

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — new builder, defaults and fallback.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — builder tests (shared with the acceptance suite).
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — read-only call site.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` default/fallback and level metadata for seeding.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — injection seam (verify; minimal or no change).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — supplies `loadDifficultyCurves()`.
